Use "jsonFile.good()". It will check for all error state flags rather than just checking the file is opened or not.
Here why are we ignoring cipher which is greater than maxCSRecords(16)? Because I can see cipher value greater than 16 in cipher_list.json.

Yes. As per IPMI spec.section 23.2, Table 23, parameter 24, user can update cipher ID only up to 16 (So default and user settings CS privilege file have 16 cipher IDs for each channel). However as per cipher list, it can be more than 16. So we may have to consider default value if supported cipher ID more than 16.
nit: please remove this empty line
Limit the try catch only to parsing.

this should probably have a try/catch in there in case record is not the shape that is expected (index "cipher" does not exist because the json file is corrupt). I agree this should never happen, but it will and then ipmid will crash.

This is supposed to return a privilege level. I see you are returning CC codes in cases of error, but returning a valid privilege level in case of success.

Please ensure that you are returning privilege levels only.
which privilege level should it return in case of error?
May be "PRIVILEGE_ERROR" or something like that

this is insufficient to fully test this feature. ipmitool does not have an option to specify wildcards in the payload types fields; it hard-codes 8 every time. This will only return the highest privilege for THIS cipher suite. Which is fine, but that means the implementation is not correct.

Where is the cipher suite info (payload types)? This function needs to return the max privilege for a given cipher suite. This should check the payload types against allowed cipher suites and then choose the correct cipher suite and max privilege for that cipher suite.

This implementation, as is, could possibly return a higher max privilege for a cipher suite that was not requested.
I don't see anywhere in this code where this function actually gets called.
can we use diferent error code ?
Every new error code has to be defined and compared.
define this in header file with macro
This will be error in casting privilege.
these should use names instead of numbers.
If somebody wants to use other configurations we might need these 20 configs

It is not so easy as just wanting to support one of the others. They would have to implement it in netipmid which would be the first clue to me that they are doing something insecure, and I would take that chance to convince them to do otherwise. Really, having all 20 of these is a waste of space.
there is no need to call this if data is null; move this below the check.
unless this is getting used by other cpp files, there is no need to have it in this header file.
